title: nf-core/sativa pipeline parameters
description: This pipeline checks sequences for their phylogenetic signal against their taxonomy

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

taxonomy.description: Path to a taxonomy file. If omitted, taxonomy is derived from --sequences record headers instead.
taxonomy.help_text: TSV file with two columns: Name and semicolon-separated taxonomy. If not given, each --sequences FASTA record's header must carry the taxonomy directly after its id (GTDB-style: `>id taxonomy;string`). If both are given, the file wins -- a warning is logged if header text is also present and being ignored.

sequences.description: Path to a sequences file, aligned or not, in phylip (.phy), Clustal (.aln) or fasta format (.fa, .fasta, .mfa, .alnfaa or .alnfna).
sequences.help_text: Unaligned content is aligned automatically via hmmalign -- see --hmm/--hmm_name.

hmm.description: Path to an HMM profile database, used to align --sequences via hmmalign if it turns out to be unaligned. Only required when the input is unaligned.
hmm.help_text: Not needed at all if --sequences is already a multiple sequence alignment (detected automatically). If the database holds more than one named profile, also set --hmm_name.

hmm_name.description: Name of the specific profile to use from --hmm, if that database holds more than one (e.g. Barrnap's databases hold one profile per rRNA gene).

skip_raxtax.description: Skip the raxtax prefilter and run every sequence straight through the full EPA-ng-based placement pipeline.

raxtax_filter_rank.description: Taxonomic rank at which raxtax's self-classification must agree with the declared taxonomy, counted from the most specific rank (1) upward. A sequence disagreeing at this one rank is flagged as a mislabel and skips EPA-ng placement.

skip_gapfilter.description: For already-aligned input: skip filtering out sequences with too high a proportion of alignment gaps, and run every sequence straight through the rest of the pipeline.

min_nongap.description: For already-aligned input: minimum proportion of non-gap columns a sequence must have in the alignment to be kept. Sequences below this are too short/incomplete to place reliably, and are reported separately instead of being placed.
min_nongap.help_text: A taxonomically broad reference alignment is naturally wide, with many columns that are only real sequence for a handful of divergent taxa -- a low default keeps that from penalising genuinely full-length sequences. Raise it for a narrower (e.g. single-genus) alignment where a stricter threshold makes sense. Only applies to input that was already aligned on entry -- see --min_profile_cover for hmmalign-derived input.

skip_profile_cover.description: For hmmalign-derived input: skip filtering out sequences that cover too little of the HMM profile, and run every sequence straight through the rest of the pipeline.

min_profile_cover.description: For hmmalign-derived input: minimum proportion of the HMM profile's match-state columns a sequence must cover to be kept. Sequences below this are too short/incomplete to place reliably, and are reported separately instead of being placed.
min_profile_cover.help_text: Unlike an already-aligned reference set, a masked hmmalign-derived alignment's width is fixed by the HMM profile itself, so real full-length sequences cluster tightly near full coverage -- a higher default than --min_nongap correctly separates them from genuinely partial sequences instead of barely filtering anything.

skip_sativa.description: Skip the phylogenetic placement subworkflow (reference tree, leave-one-out placement, scoring) entirely.
skip_sativa.help_text: Turns the rest of the pipeline into a general-purpose taxonomy-resolution/alignment/prefilter QC tool: taxonomy resolution, name-consistency checking, optional alignment (via hmmalign) and gap/profile-coverage filtering, and the optional raxtax prefilter all still run as configured. The final mislabels report then contains only raxtax-flagged mislabels (or is empty if --skip_raxtax is also set) -- no EPA-ng-based placement is performed. The cleaned, filtered alignment and taxonomy are still published, under whichever upstream step (raxtax prefilter, gap/profile-coverage filter, or name-consistency check) produced them last.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
